title: PLT legislation list
description: A jurisdiction's list of pesticide legislation. A case is selected when any instrument on the list is named in its title, abstract, subject fields or full text. There is no scoring, no gating and no exclusion pattern: an instrument either belongs on the list, in which case a judgment that names it is a pesticide case, or it does not.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema. 1.0.0 is the first legislation-list schema; it succeeds keywords-2.0.0, whose terms were substances, product classes, crops and practices as well as statutes, and whose 'requires' gates and 'exclusions' patterns this schema deliberately does not carry.

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, or EU for the European Union.

list_version.description: Semantic version of THIS list. Stored with every match, so bump it on every change that can alter what is selected or how it is labelled. Bump the minor version when instruments are added or removed, the major version when matching semantics change, the patch version for a change that cannot alter selection.

languages.description: ISO 639-1 codes of the languages this list carries names in. The number forms of Union instruments are language-independent and are not a language.

sources.description: Where the generated part of the list came from and when it was read. The hand-curated part is its own provenance: every entry says in 'note' why it is here.

fields.description: Document fields an instrument is looked for in, in this order. A field not named here is not scanned: this is the curator's decision about what counts as the text of a judgment.

terms.description: The instruments. Called terms because that is what they are to the matcher: a name and the spellings it is cited under.

then.$comment: A regex term's 'term' is a pattern, and a pattern is not a name. Since every match is shown to the public as a label, a regex term has to say what to call it.

id.description: Stable identifier, prefixed with the language code. Never reuse an id for a different instrument; match provenance is stored against it, and it labels every case the instrument selected.

term.description: The instrument's short citation as a court writes it, in the source language. Also the public label a case carries when it matches, unless 'label' overrides it.

label.description: What to call this instrument where a reader sees it: on the case page, in the case-list filter, in a match report. Defaults to 'term'. Required when 'match' is 'regex'.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 code of the language 'term' is written in. Aliases may be in any language the list carries.

category.description: What kind of instrument this is. Stored on every match, so it is the second label a case carries and the one the public filters by. Union acts are typed as EUR-Lex types them; national instruments as their own legal order does.

match.description: 'word' matches on word boundaries; 'phrase' matches a whitespace-normalised multi-word sequence, and is what a citation form wants; 'substring' matches anywhere (for compounding languages, six characters at least); 'regex' for the rare case the others cannot express.

case_sensitive.description: Set true only for short acronyms whose lowercase form is a common word. Inherited by every alias, so a case_sensitive term carries acronyms only.

case_sensitive_exception.description: Opts this term out of the acronym-only rule enforced on case_sensitive terms. The loader rejects it on a term that is not case_sensitive, and on one that does not need it.

aliases.description: The other citation forms and names of THIS instrument: its number in the bracketed and suffixed forms of every language, its title in each language the list carries, its customary short name. An alias is reported under this term's id and label, so a different instrument is never an alias: it is its own term.

celex.description: CELEX number of a Union instrument, as EUR-Lex identifies it. Provenance, not a pattern: nothing matches on it.

bwb.description: Identifier of a Dutch instrument in the Basiswettenbestand, as wetten.overheid.nl identifies it. Provenance, not a pattern.

title.description: The instrument's full official title, for the reader of the list. Not matched: courts cite the number or the short name.

derived_from.description: CELEX number of the base instrument this act was enumerated under by scripts/legislation_from_cellar.py. Present on every generated entry and absent from every hand-curated one, which is how the script knows which entries are its own to replace.
